sources.entry: Work the exercises in Performance Ninja alongside them; reading alone will not build the instinct.

summary.one_liner: Performance Ninja is a hands-on online course of C++ lab assignments for finding and fixing low-level CPU performance problems such as cache misses and branch mispredictions.
summary.what_it_does: The course is organized as lab assignments plus YouTube videos, with students spending most of their time analyzing and optimizing code. Labs are grouped into categories: Core Bound (vectorization, function inlining, dependency chains, compiler intrinsics), Memory Bound (data packing, loop interchange, loop tiling, software prefetching, false sharing, huge pages, memory alignment), Bad Speculation (branches to CMOVs, conditional stores, lookup tables, C++ virtual calls), and Misc (warmup, LTO, PGO, optimizing IO). Each lab takes roughly 30 minutes to 4 hours. Solutions are submitted to GitHub for automated benchmarking and verification. The README says the labs run on Linux, Windows, and Mac across several recent CPUs, including Intel Alder Lake, AMD Zen 3, and Apple M1. Ports to Rust (perf-ninja-rs) and Zig (perf-ninja-zig) are mentioned.
use_cases: learn cpu performance optimization through exercises
practice fixing cache misses and branch mispredictions
loop interchange and loop tiling exercises
automated benchmarking of optimized C++ code
preparing for low-level performance analysis work
how_to_run: Read the Get Started page in the repository before starting labs
Watch the warmup video referenced in the README
Work through the lab assignments in C++
Submit your solution to GitHub for automated benchmarking and verification
notable: Hands-on lab format where most time is spent profiling and improving code
Automated benchmarking and verification via GitHub submission
Covers Core Bound, Memory Bound, Bad Speculation, and Misc performance topics
Runs on Linux, Windows, and Mac across Intel, AMD, and Apple M1 hardware
Free course with community ports to Rust and Zig
caveats: Basic C++ skills are required; knowledge of compilers, computer architecture, and assembly reading is a plus
The README describes the project as a work in progress, with the CPU Frontend Bound and Data-Driven sections currently empty
Lab time ranges from 30 minutes to 4 hours each
